solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drug distributor checks guy removing coat

indicators.note: to check something is to hold it back, so one piece is held inside the other

explanation.surface: A dealer handing out drugs keeps an eye on some fellow who is taking off his jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: The coat is a fleece, not a jacket: the man removing it from a sheep is a shearer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shearer is a man who clips the woolly fleece off sheep, a cryptic picture of removing an animal's coat.

clue.text: No special favourites where this child is raised

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising something lifts it upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for special
favourites are pets, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A household where the parents raising this child play no favourites.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at a blended family treating every child alike, which suits the answer neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is a child, the son of one's husband or wife from an earlier relationship.

clue.text: Prominent fellow denied beginning to bury bomb

indicators.note: burying puts something inside, so the explosive goes into the shortened word
refused its start, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: A notable man, refused a start, digs in a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent describes someone distinguished and well known, a synonym for prominent.

clue.text: Take covers off iron posts for bed

indicators.note: removing the covers strips the outside letters from each of the next words

explanation.surface: Instructions to strip the casing from iron posts to make a bedframe.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is where birds sleep, so it is their bed; the verb sense of going to bed also fits.

clue.text: Stomach ulcer — I must somehow bar sulphur

indicators.note: somehow means in some unexplained way, so the letters can come in any order
to bar is to exclude, so the chemical element is shut out of the word

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A patient with a stomach ulcer is told to give up sulphur in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: Take S from MUST to leave MUT, then rearrange it with ULCER and I.
explanation.definitionFit: The reticulum is the second chamber of a ruminant's stomach, so it is a stomach in its own right.

clue.text: Austere and vinegary, masking trace of sugar

indicators.note: masking means covering, so the first word wraps round the small piece

parts.note: acetic acid is the acid in vinegar

indicators.note: a trace is only the slightest part, so take just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Something strict and sour, with just a hint of sweetness hidden in it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic way of life is severely self-denying, so austere is a close synonym.

clue.text: Go off alcohol-charged days? The opposite

indicators.note: charged means loaded, so one piece is filled with the other
this reverses the stated roles, so the alcohol holds the days rather than the days holding the alcohol

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Swear off booze for days of heavy drinking, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The opposite' flips the stated order: rather than days charged with alcohol, the alcohol is charged with days.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs addle when they go rotten, so the verb means to spoil or go bad.

clue.text: Stupidly opt to be out of range of total eclipse? It's sublime

indicators.note: done stupidly means done in a muddled way, so the remaining letters are rearranged

indicators.text: to be out of range of
indicators.note: being out of range means absent from the set, so those letters are struck out

explanation.surface: Foolishly choosing to miss the path of a total eclipse, which is a heavenly spectacle.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial means heavenly, and heavenly things are figuratively sublime or exalted.

clue.text: Instruments of terror briefly employed by regressive university

indicators.note: regressive means moving backwards, so the university's name is read in reverse

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

indicators.note: made brief, the word is cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: Fearsome instruments of torture once used by a backward-looking college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instruments of terror' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at Instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are kettledrums, the large tuned percussion instruments of an orchestra.

clue.text: Provision for masses of tea with new judge

parts.note: cha or char is British slang for tea
N is the abbreviation for new
to try a case is to judge it

explanation.surface: Catering for crowds with tea and a fresh judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masses' suggests crowds, but these are church masses.
explanation.definitionFit: A chantry is an endowment paying for masses to be sung for the founder's soul, or the chapel built for them.

clue.text: Remove something from wordplay for "diet"?

parts.note: surface reading: a fragment of a clue that leads to the word diet
setter's reading: a four-letter word for alter or revise, followed by a common anagram signal, rearranges into diet

explanation.surface: A puzzle-maker's note about trimming part of a clue for the word diet.
explanation.walkthrough: EDIT OUT read as two words is itself a clue to DIET: EDIT, followed by the anagram signal OUT, shuffles to DIET. So the answer both means remove and is the wordplay described.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit something out of a text or film is to cut it, so the phrase means remove.

clue.text: Cover over woman in novel predicament

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word for cover is read backwards

parts.note: Emma is the heroine of Jane Austen's novel

explanation.surface: A book's cover showing a woman caught in a tricky situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult choice between options, which is a kind of predicament.

clue.text: Performance aspect a clergyman suppresses

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down out of sight, so the answer lies concealed within the next few words

parts.note: letters run on from the end of aspect through a into the start of clergyman

explanation.surface: Some feature of a show that a priest wants kept quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a grand public show or display, so it is a kind of performance.

clue.text: Little John captured by opening to Sherwood Forest at last

indicators.note: something captured is held inside, so the word for John goes between the two single letters
an opening is the start of something, so only the first letter of Sherwood is used

parts.note: John and can are both slang for a toilet

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of Forest

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's Little John taken prisoner at the edge of Sherwood Forest.
explanation.walkthrough: Little John is Robin Hood's companion, but here Little is the definition and John is the US slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient, so it can stand for little as an adjective.

clue.text: Chemical certain to be returned decarbonised and inactive

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards
C is the symbol for carbon, so taking the carbon out removes that letter
read as in-active, it asks for the abbreviation for active to be taken out

explanation.surface: A chemical sure to be sent back once its carbon is removed and it is no longer reactive.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C (carbon) and A (active, as in grammar) from CERTAIN to leave ERTIN, then reverse it. 'Inactive' looks like a synonym for inert, a tempting anagram of the answer, but it is a deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is potassium nitrate, saltpetre, a chemical compound used in gunpowder.

clue.text: Model almost ruins peace of Greek philosopher

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so the letters are formed into something new
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A model's behaviour nearly destroys a Greek thinker's tranquillity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a noun, a fashion model, but it is a verb telling you to reshape the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicurean is the adjective from Epicurus, the Greek philosopher who taught that pleasure and calm are the highest good.

clue.text: Troublemaker regularly lacking flair and talent

indicators.note: losing letters at regular intervals leaves only every other letter of the word

parts.note: second and fourth letters of flair

explanation.surface: A disruptive person who often has neither style nor skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A liability is a person or thing that causes trouble or puts others at a disadvantage.

clue.text: We cannot recall resolving main cases

indicators.note: resolving can mean breaking something down into its parts and reforming it

explanation.surface: Detectives admit they can't remember solving the principal cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesiacs are people suffering memory loss, so they might say of themselves that they cannot remember.

clue.text: Somebody peeled Jimmy's jamming fruit

indicators.note: jamming means squeezing in, so the shortened name is pushed inside the first word
peeling takes off the skin, so the outer letters of the name are removed

parts.note: the name, before its first and last letters come off

explanation.surface: Some person has stripped the skin from Jimmy's fruit for making jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jamming' suggests preserves, fitting fruit, but it means squeezing in.
explanation.definitionFit: A persimmon is an orange tomato-like fruit from an East Asian tree.

clue.text: Piaf churned up inside about contralto in command presentation of La Mer

definitions.note: a sea's name for a French phrase meaning the sea

indicators.note: the mixed letters sit about the voice letter, placing it inside them
churning stirs things vigorously, so the singer's name is mixed up

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for contralto
i/c is short for in charge or in command

explanation.surface: Edith Piaf, moved, singing low at a royal performance of the song La Mer.
explanation.walkthrough: La Mer is a famous French chanson, which suits Piaf, but here it is just French for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific is the world's largest ocean, an example of the sea that la mer names.

clue.text: What publisher pays Prince Harry?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a payment to an author for each copy sold
second meaning: the royal family, of which Harry is a member

explanation.surface: Wondering how much a publisher paid Prince Harry for his memoir.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Harry's memoir deal; the question mark flags that Harry is an example of the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an author's share of book sales and royal persons collectively, of whom the prince is one.

clue.text: Stripper spending time here?

definitions.note: an adverb standing for a noun: the locus is the place one means by here

indicators.note: spending something uses it up, so the letter for time is lost

parts.note: a locust swarm strips crops bare
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Asking whether a striptease artist does her shifts in this venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The stripper is not a dancer but an insect that strips vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: A locus is a particular position or place, the spot meant when one says here.

clue.text: Kremlin directed a non-voluntary movement in revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Moscow's seat of power steered an unwilling uprising during the revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kremlin is the fortified inner citadel of Moscow; kremlin is Russian for such a fortress.

clue.text: Feeble creditors taking up the lowest of debts

indicators.text: taking up the lowest of debts
indicators.note: in a down entry the lowest letter is at the bottom, and taking it up moves it to the top

parts.note: creditors are those who lend money

explanation.surface: Weak lenders take on the worst of the bad debts.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the bottom letter, S, the final letter both of debts and of the lenders' word, to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender can mean slight or weak, as in slender hopes or a slender chance.

clue.text: Shy, puny, half-cut, rat-like individual

indicators.note: cut in half means only one half of the word is kept, here the front

explanation.surface: A timid, weak, somewhat drunk person with a ratty look about him.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for tipsy, but here it means cut to half.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American water rodent, a beaver-sized animal resembling a rat.

clue.text: Withdraw from case of exhausted Ukrainian woman plugged by US police

indicators.note: an exhausted thing is emptied out, so only the outside letters of Ukrainian remain

parts.note: first and last letters of Ukrainian

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so the police word goes inside the word for woman

parts.note: a woman referred to as she
the heat is American slang for the police

explanation.surface: A tired Ukrainian woman, caught up by American cops, pulls out of a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: The case is a scabbard, not a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsheathe a sword is to draw it out of its scabbard or protective case.

clue.text: Loose relative paraded topless

indicators.note: without its top, a down word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A wild relative walked about without a top on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' sounds like it describes the relative's morals, but it is the verb to set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose a knot or a captive is to untie or release it.

clue.text: Period during which Copernicus held back

indicators.note: held back reads as kept in reverse order, so the letters run backwards
during means within the span of, so the answer lies inside the following words

parts.note: the end of which and start of Copernicus

explanation.surface: The era when Copernicus kept his theory to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Copernicus's work began a new era in astronomy.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a distinct period of time or historical era.

clue.text: Least bright, given fresh start, becomes most rounded

indicators.note: a new start replaces the old one, so the first letter of the word is swapped
the start of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: The dimmest pupil, given a second chance, turns out the most well-rounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Fullest describes the plumpest or most completely filled out, like the most rounded figure or moon.

clue.text: Missed nothing boring enthusiastic editor

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the nothing goes inside the next word

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Nothing slipped past the keen editor, though dull work was involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like dull, describing the nothing, but it means piercing.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoided, as in steered clear of, matches missed in the sense of dodged.

clue.text: Spice Islands cropped unlimited fennel

indicators.note: cropping trims off the end, so the last letter goes
without its limits the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: The Spice Islands' crops include fennel grown without restriction.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spice Islands are the Moluccas, but here Spice is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is a hot red pepper ground into a spice.

clue.text: Schoenberg contributing more than Larsson to development of pupil

indicators.note: both names give only their opening letters, the first giving a greater share than the second

explanation.surface: The composer Schoenberg did more than Larsson to shape a student's growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar was once simply a schoolchild or student, an older sense of pupil.
